concepts.name: Non-relational data store idea
concepts.summary: Can state that NoSQL stores hold data in models other than fixed-schema relational tables and name why they emerged.

concepts.name: Key-value model
concepts.summary: Can explain that data is stored and retrieved as opaque values looked up by a unique key.

concepts.name: Document model
concepts.summary: Can explain that records are self-contained, nested documents (such as JSON) grouped into collections.

concepts.name: Wide-column model
concepts.summary: Can describe rows identified by keys holding sparse, flexible sets of columns grouped into column families.

concepts.name: Graph model
concepts.summary: Can describe data as nodes and relationships with properties, suited to highly connected data.

concepts.name: Flexible schema
concepts.summary: Can explain that records in one collection may have different fields and the structure is enforced by the application rather than the database.

concepts.name: Matching model to use case
concepts.summary: Can match typical examples (caching, catalogues, time series, social networks) to the NoSQL family that fits them.

misconceptions.text: NoSQL means the database can never use SQL-like query languages or has no structure at all.
All NoSQL databases work the same way and are interchangeable.
A flexible schema means the data has no schema at all.

concepts.name: CRUD operations on documents
concepts.summary: Can insert, read, update and delete documents and key-value entries using a store's basic API or shell.

concepts.name: Query filters and projections
concepts.summary: Can write queries with conditions, sorting, limits and field projections against a document collection.

concepts.name: Primary keys and partition keys
concepts.summary: Can explain that the key determines how records are located and distributed, and choose a sensible key for simple cases.

concepts.name: Embedding versus referencing
concepts.summary: Can model a one-to-many relationship either by embedding child data in a parent document or by storing references.

concepts.name: Secondary indexes
concepts.summary: Can create an index on a non-key field to speed up a query and recognise its write and storage cost.

concepts.name: Basic graph traversal queries
concepts.summary: Can write a simple query that matches nodes and follows relationships to find connected items.

concepts.name: Replication and sharding terms
concepts.summary: Can explain that replication copies data for availability and sharding splits data across nodes for scale.

misconceptions.text: Queries in a document database are fast on any field without any indexing.
Embedding is always better than referencing because there are no joins.
Replication and sharding are the same thing.

concepts.name: Query-driven data modelling
concepts.summary: Can derive a data model from the application's list of queries rather than from entity normalisation.

concepts.name: Denormalisation and duplication trade-offs
concepts.summary: Can analyse where duplicating data speeds reads and what update-consistency burden it creates.

concepts.name: CAP theorem
concepts.summary: Can analyse what a system must give up between consistency and availability during a network partition.

concepts.name: Eventual versus strong consistency
concepts.summary: Can explain and compare eventual and strong consistency and predict what reads may return after writes.

concepts.name: Partition key selection
concepts.summary: Can analyse a candidate partition key for even distribution, query locality and hot-spot risk.

concepts.name: Aggregation pipelines
concepts.summary: Can build multi-stage aggregations that filter, group and transform documents.

concepts.name: Single-document atomicity and transactions
concepts.summary: Can analyse which operations are atomic by default and when multi-record transactions are needed or costly.

concepts.name: Relational versus NoSQL selection
concepts.summary: Can compare relational and NoSQL options for a scenario on structure, queries, consistency and scale.

misconceptions.text: You should model NoSQL data by normalising entities first, exactly as in a relational design.
CAP means a system permanently picks only two of consistency, availability and partition tolerance.
NoSQL databases do not support transactions or atomic operations at all.

concepts.name: Tunable consistency and quorums
concepts.summary: Can reason about replica counts and read/write quorum settings to tune consistency against latency and availability.

concepts.name: Consistent hashing and rebalancing
concepts.summary: Can analyse how consistent hashing places data and limits movement when nodes join or leave.

concepts.name: Storage engines and LSM trees
concepts.summary: Can analyse how LSM-based and B-tree storage engines trade write throughput, read cost and compaction.

concepts.name: Conflict resolution strategies
concepts.summary: Can evaluate approaches to resolving concurrent writes and their risk of data loss or complexity.

concepts.name: PACELC and latency trade-offs
concepts.summary: Can evaluate how a system trades latency against consistency even when there is no partition.

concepts.name: Index and query performance diagnosis
concepts.summary: Can use query plans and metrics to diagnose slow queries and fix indexing or model problems.

concepts.name: Polyglot persistence design
concepts.summary: Can evaluate combining several data stores in one system and the cost of keeping them in sync.

concepts.name: Schema evolution and migration
concepts.summary: Can evaluate strategies for changing document structure in live systems without downtime or inconsistency.

misconceptions.text: Setting quorums to majority always guarantees linearizable reads.
Last-write-wins is a safe default because it never loses data.
Consistency trade-offs only matter during network partitions.

concepts.name: Architecture selection under constraints
concepts.summary: Can judge and defend a data store choice against workload, consistency, cost, operational and team constraints.

concepts.name: Distributed correctness reasoning
concepts.summary: Can evaluate a system's guarantees against anomalies such as stale reads, lost updates and write skew.

concepts.name: Multi-region replication design
concepts.summary: Can design a multi-region topology balancing latency, failover, data residency and conflict handling.

concepts.name: Capacity and scaling strategy
concepts.summary: Can create a plan for growth covering sharding, rebalancing, hot-key mitigation and cost.

concepts.name: Event-driven derived data pipelines
concepts.summary: Can design pipelines that propagate changes into search, cache and analytic views with defined consistency.

concepts.name: Failure and resilience testing
concepts.summary: Can evaluate durability and recovery behaviour through failure scenarios, backups and restore drills.

concepts.name: Custom data model frameworks
concepts.summary: Can create reusable modelling patterns and governance guidelines for teams working with NoSQL stores.

misconceptions.text: Horizontal scaling a NoSQL database is automatic and needs no data model or key design effort.
Multi-region replication improves availability without any consistency or latency cost.
Derived stores populated from change streams are always immediately consistent with the source.
